text: Build collections of modular components (head, body, hair, clothing) and compose them by hand or procedurally using Blueprints. Optimized face textures that maintain visual fidelity with reduced memory footprint. Animation applied using Unreal Animation Framework or simple sequences depending on distance. Simulated with Mass, rendered using Nanite or dynamic LOD systems. Example project setup available separately, runs on all Unreal Engine target platforms. For more information on this feature, see MetaHuman Crowds. Convert any human character mesh with arbitrary topology into a fully-rigged MetaHuman in a single workflow. This improved Mesh to MetaHuman process conforms both head and body simultaneously, accepting input meshes of any topology and automatically generating results powered by the MetaHuman database. Combined head and body conforming in a single step. Accepts head and/or body mesh of any topology as input. Automatic results for human characters with manual control available for technical fixes. Ideal for characters created from scans, external GenAI/DCC tools, or existing character conversions. Designed for humanoid characters only; the resulting character will adopt the MetaHuman topology and rig. For more information on this feature, see From Custom Mesh. Assemble MetaHuman characters without baked materials and textures. This allows granular lookdev and texture control for artists wanting to match a specific look. Author unbaked texture and material assets using standard Unreal Engine editors or export textures to external DCC tools. Options are provided to then override with user-customized textures and materials in MetaHuman Creator. Full control over textures and materials for custom visual fidelity or aesthetic styles. Modified unbaked materials and textures can be applied as overrides in the MetaHuman Creator for users to still benefit from the material baking when running default assemblies. Standard Unreal Engine workflow using familiar asset editors. Use Case: Enables looks beyond MetaHuman Creator's built-in capabilities while maintaining performance optimization. Create custom lighting scenes in MetaHuman Creator to preview characters in the context of your target environment. Define lighting setups using templates that include skydome hemispheres, post-processing volumes, and light groups, then use these custom scenes to validate visual fidelity while authoring. Preview characters in your target lighting environment directly in MetaHuman Creator. Close the gap between MetaHuman Creator previews and in-level appearance. Inspect and modify viewport render settings for precise control.
title: Unreal Engine 5.8 Release Notes

text: Define lighting setups using templates that include skydome hemispheres, post-processing volumes, and light groups, then use these custom scenes to validate visual fidelity while authoring. Preview characters in your target lighting environment directly in MetaHuman Creator. Close the gap between MetaHuman Creator previews and in-level appearance. Inspect and modify viewport render settings for precise control. Ideal for character artists, lighting artists, and lookdev teams. MetaHuman Creator viewport now fully supports Lumen too. Custom scenes use templates rather than importing full-game levels; results may still require iterative refinement to match the exact in-engine appearance. Capture body, or face and body performance, for a single actor from a single camera. This new experimental capability extends the accessibility of MetaHuman Animator from faces to bodies, removing the optical motion-capture stage as a barrier for content creators. Available as a standalone plugin on Fab and integrated directly into MetaHuman Animator, with the Live Link Face mobile apps updated to support body capture alongside face. Body capture for a single actor from a single camera, with optional simultaneous face capture. Compatible with a wide range of consumer hardware including webcams and supported smartphones. Available as a standalone MetaHuman Animator Markerless Motion Capture plugin via Fab, and integrated as a capability of MetaHuman Animator inside Unreal Engine. For more information on this feature, see Animation from Mono Video Capture. MetaHuman Animator offers an improved API for batch processing large volumes of captured performance data. The updated workflow covers the full pipeline, end to end, from solve through animation review and export. Reference Blueprint examples will be included to extend or customize for your specific pipeline. MetaHuman Animator now supports Linux and macOS, expanding the availability of the Unreal Engine editor and MetaHuman Creator across platforms. You can generate facial animation from performance capture on Linux and macOS, without requiring access to a Windows machine. However, body animation features are currently only available on Windows. Offline and real-time facial MetaHuman Animator functionality available on Linux and macOS. Platform parity with Unreal Engine editor and MetaHuman Creator. Real-time facial animation on Linux is only available using Live Link Face. Editor-only solution; not a runtime or player-facing feature.
title: Unreal Engine 5.8 Release Notes

text: You can generate facial animation from performance capture on Linux and macOS, without requiring access to a Windows machine. However, body animation features are currently only available on Windows. Offline and real-time facial MetaHuman Animator functionality available on Linux and macOS. Platform parity with Unreal Engine editor and MetaHuman Creator. Real-time facial animation on Linux is only available using Live Link Face. Editor-only solution; not a runtime or player-facing feature. New real-time and offline animation models deliver improved solve quality across a wider range of capture conditions, including varied camera angles, lens distortion, and infrared lighting. Audio-driven animation benefits from a new real-time model. Curve output is more animator-friendly, with cleaner activation on key poses for easier editing and refinement. A next-generation mesh-based terrain solution to support large worlds using 3D modeling, layering, virtual texture, generic editor tools, variable tessellation, and Nanite. Our aim with this feature is to replace and remove the typical constraints of the current heightfield-only landscape solution in Unreal Engine. For more information about this feature, see Mesh Terrain. In the Fast Geometry Streaming plugin, we included multiple new improvements for speed, stability, and use cases support, over the initial 5.6 release. Added decal, point, spot and rect lights components support. Added support for mesh paint textures in the static mesh component. Fixed non-primitive components that were ignored from the transformation process. Root component mobility is now preserved when the FastGeo runtime cell transformer creates a new replacement root component for a transformed component. Fixed primitives incorrectly showing when running PIE and the player is ejected. Refactored to simplify/clarify the interface of the fast geometry component. Fixed the WorldPartitionRuntimeCellTransformerISM duplicating instances for Blueprint actors that were not fully transformable. Multiple additional fixes for crashes, threading, deadlocks and initialization are also part of this experimental release. We added world partition streaming debugging tools to Unreal Insights and Unreal Editor, making possible per-cell analysis and sessions playback. We made the following improvements to world partition hierarchical level of details (HLODs). Added a batched deletion operation to reduce source control overhead. Now supports standalone HLODs when placing multiple instances of the same sub-world partition level. Added a perceptual difference heuristic option to update HLODs only when needed.
title: Unreal Engine 5.8 Release Notes

text: We added world partition streaming debugging tools to Unreal Insights and Unreal Editor, making possible per-cell analysis and sessions playback. We made the following improvements to world partition hierarchical level of details (HLODs). Added a batched deletion operation to reduce source control overhead. Now supports standalone HLODs when placing multiple instances of the same sub-world partition level. Added a perceptual difference heuristic option to update HLODs only when needed. Added support for new and deleted actors when building HLODs directly from a level in the editor. Build HLOD for Selected Region through the world partition editor. In UE 5.8, we added non-destructive manual editing of PCG data and artifacts through selection, exclusion, modification and support for restoring data. Individual nodes in the graphs can be marked for manual editing or temporarily overridden. A new Data Overrides window lists all overrides applied to an inspected node. Using arrays, structures, sets, and maps as metadata attribute values and overrides are now supported. This includes various operations to extract data in structures and arrays as well as array operations. New Create Complex Constant and Add Complex Constant nodes are available to use in PCG graphs on top of graph parameters with complex types. We added support for creating custom subgraphs, similar to Blueprint functions, stored and edited directly within a PCG graph. You can now categorize, sort, group, and describe PCG parameters in the new parameters hierarchy editor tool. PCG GPU runtime scatter is now within the same performance range as the landscape GPU grass system, and was stress-tested on all platforms. Added CRC and caching improvements when running a graph, reducing potential cache invalidation with increased efficiency. Improved ISM re-use logic when spawning large sets of static meshes. Made graph execution and scheduling improvements removing contention and bottlenecks. We continue to make UX improvements when working with PCG, these are latest changes: Contextual filtering: When adding a new node by dragging from any typed pin, the node palette is automatically filtered to supported operations, with options to include conversions or disable filtering entirely. HLSL kernels: You can now create attributes directly from the HLSL kernel rather than in the node settings. HLSL editor: You can now set font size.
title: Unreal Engine 5.8 Release Notes

text: HLSL kernels: You can now create attributes directly from the HLSL kernel rather than in the node settings. HLSL editor: You can now set font size. Data viewport: You can now edit manual overrides from the PCG editor's data viewport With Unreal Engine 5.8, we also introduce multiple native PCG elements and new options including: Metadata array operations: Most useful operations for arrays (make, add, add unique, contains, and more). Align points: Snap points position and rotation against the bounds of another point on any given axis and spatial referential. Scene Capture: The Scene Capture node now supports input transforms allowing captures to be taken from any direction and adding extra flexibility for GPU sampling. Create / Add Complex Constant: Use these nodes to create or add any complex attribute type directly in the graph. Apply Spline to Component: Writes the PCG spline data onto an existing Spline component reference. Useful for applying changes on existing splines in-editor. Teleport Actors and Components: Gives you a method to apply a transform to any actor or component reference in the world. Useful for a new level-based PCG workflow to apply an instant operation in-editor. Get Class from Attribute: Gets the class from a soft object reference and returns it as an attribute. Get Editor Cameras: Returns the current visible editor viewport cameras as points to use for various in-editor operations. Set Materials On Dynamic Mesh: Apply material to dynamic mesh data. The Procedural Vegetation Editor is an experimental plugin to create and edit vegetation meshes, supporting Nanite foliage, directly within Unreal Engine. With UE 5.8, we introduce some core new functionality that greatly expands the capabilities of PVE, enabling growth directly in the editor without the need for imported recipes, along with numerous other improvements. Skeletal Extraction from 3D Mesh or 2D image/Atlas For more information on this feature, see Procedural Vegetation Editor. State Tree gets a flexibility boost in UE 5.8. We improved authoring workflows; trees can now define their starting state. A new Compiler Manager helps streamline iteration, and the editor now tracks when trees are out of date so it’s clearer when a recompile is needed.
title: Unreal Engine 5.8 Release Notes

text: Skeletal Extraction from 3D Mesh or 2D image/Atlas For more information on this feature, see Procedural Vegetation Editor. State Tree gets a flexibility boost in UE 5.8. We improved authoring workflows; trees can now define their starting state. A new Compiler Manager helps streamline iteration, and the editor now tracks when trees are out of date so it’s clearer when a recompile is needed. Property binding is more robust and now allows binding to be easily reversed, making it straightforward to move data from one completed task to another. For more information on this feature, see Statetree. Mass, our data-oriented entity system, gets a major overhaul. Mass Signals are now part of the core engine, and entities can be created off the game thread thanks to archetype-based, lock-free scheduling. A new sparse/virtual fragment system reduces memory use and allows optional fragments and tags to be added or removed without triggering costly archetype changes. We completely overhauled Mass processor execution and dependency resolution to better take advantage of multi-core CPUs, resulting in safer and faster execution on modern hardware. This is supported by more granular scheduling and thread-safe observer notifications. A new MassCore module further simplifies adoption by separating the core entity system from the broader MassGameplay stack. For more information on this feature, see MassEntity. Static meshes can now define their own walkable areas during navmesh generation, giving designers more control over how AI navigates the world. You can assign per-mesh area costs to static geometry—for example, marking a couch so AI prefers to walk around it instead of over it. This is enabled per mesh through a flag and area class setting on NavCollision, with support carried through the full Recast generation pipeline. Iris is now production-ready for licensees in UE 5.8. Alongside that milestone, we added a range of improvements that focus on stability and day-to-day usability. We improved protocol mismatch handling so clients get clearer errors when out of sync with the server, and new warnings help catch object lifecycle issues earlier. Serialization, cull distance handling, and diagnostics have all been refined, and RPC DoS detection has been re-enabled. Iris also moves closer to the engine’s broader direction, with added support for Scene Graph integration and RemoteObjects RPC routing.
title: Unreal Engine 5.8 Release Notes

text: We improved protocol mismatch handling so clients get clearer errors when out of sync with the server, and new warnings help catch object lifecycle issues earlier. Serialization, cull distance handling, and diagnostics have all been refined, and RPC DoS detection has been re-enabled. Iris also moves closer to the engine’s broader direction, with added support for Scene Graph integration and RemoteObjects RPC routing. For more information on this feature, see Iris Replication System. Mover receives a broad update across core movement, networking, animation, and ChaosMover. Core movement modes get a wide range of fixes and improvements, including NavWalking support for Detour Crowd, better based movement for scenarios like moving platforms or rocking boats, and improved root motion and montage handling. Layered moves can now be scheduled ahead of time for better synchronization, while rollback and prediction support have been expanded. Networking also improves with optional Iris replication support in Network Prediction and adaptive time dilation to reduce client predict-ahead. ChaosMover adds trajectory prediction for motion-matching workflows, deeper Chaos Visual Debugger integration, and broader support for sim-driven montages, layered moves, gameplay tags, and instant movement effects. Together, these changes continue the architectural work toward moving Mover out of Experimental status while improving stability across movement modes, prediction, resimulation, and animation-driven workflows. We streamlined input workflows in UE 5.8 with the unification of Enhanced Input and Common Input/UI. This simplifies cross-platform input handling, removes the need for duplicate data assets, and makes debugging more straightforward. The update also includes a range of improvements across input handling, including more reliable event processing, better widget binding behavior, expanded virtual key support, and fixes for trigger edge cases. New tooling, such as an Input Debugger for Enhanced Input UI and added extensibility, makes it easier to build and troubleshoot input-driven experiences. Incremental Cooking continues as a beta feature for UE 5.8. Improvements to determinism further reduces the need to recook unmodified assets notably with DDC and structured data variations. Incremental Cooking helps you to iterate faster on your target devices by reducing overall cooking time. Cook processes automatically analyze asset changes against output stored in Zen Server and only cook new updates made to your project's assets. This works across all native engine assets including Blueprints and World Partition tiles.
title: Unreal Engine 5.8 Release Notes

text: Improvements to determinism further reduces the need to recook unmodified assets notably with DDC and structured data variations. Incremental Cooking helps you to iterate faster on your target devices by reducing overall cooking time. Cook processes automatically analyze asset changes against output stored in Zen Server and only cook new updates made to your project's assets. This works across all native engine assets including Blueprints and World Partition tiles. Zenserver as Cooked Output Store is now enabled by default. This also has meaning for Zenserver Streaming being used automatically by workflows in Unreal Editor when launching the game / client on devices, and staging container files (pak / iostore) remains available and supported for non-iteration workflows. To ensure this functions with remote devices, Zenserver responds to remote requests, but only if they supply a pre-generated key for authorization. Existing projects that have the use of Zen store disabled in their project settings will not use Zenserver as a cooked output store. They will need to manually change the setting in the project settings to enable it. For professional development use cases, projects should set LimitProcessLifetime=false in the Zen.AutoLaunch section of the DefaultEngine.ini configuration file so that Zenserver is not starting and stopping frequently. This requires consideration from automated / build processes to ensure that Zenserver continuing to run happens in a way that doesn’t interfere with automated / build processes. The AllowRemoteNetworkService config key has been renamed and changed to RemoteNetworkService and doesn’t accept true / false, and instead uses the following values: None rejects remote requests to the local UE-launched Zenserver. Unsecured accepts remote requests to the local UE-launched Zenserver if they contain an authorization key in their header that matches a UE-generated key. For more information on this topic, see Zenserver as Cooked Output Store and Zenserver Streaming. Improvements to Horde Analytics tooling continues in UE 5.8 as an Experimental feature with improvements to dashboard UX for job steps (CPU, memory usage) and job health observability. We've also introduced a new view in Horde which shows runtime trends outputted from the Automated Performance Tests framework (APT) and the Perf Report Tool (csvprofilers), highlighting key metrics such as GPU/CPU times, peak memory usage and hitch reports so regressions can be spotted.
title: Unreal Engine 5.8 Release Notes

text: We've also introduced a new view in Horde which shows runtime trends outputted from the Automated Performance Tests framework (APT) and the Perf Report Tool (csvprofilers), highlighting key metrics such as GPU/CPU times, peak memory usage and hitch reports so regressions can be spotted. This currently relies on users having their own database store model. Audio Insights received a big update with new features and improvements in UE 5.8, expanding its diagnostic capabilities across loudness metering, signal flow visualization, live event monitoring, and data plotting — alongside numerous stability, UX, and standalone app improvements. Loudness Metering: A dedicated loudness meter tracks momentary, short-term, and integrated loudness values along with loudness range and true peak values, target max values and clipping indicators, processed on the engine and streamed into both the editor and standalone app. Signal Flow Visualizer: A new tab that traces the instantaneous audio signal graph from its source through submixes to the output device, displaying mixing values at each stage to find attenuation or routing issues. Displays cached data as well for offline forensic analysis. Timeline Cache Controls: Dynamic controls over display playhead synchronizing data display for a single timestamp across several dashboards of data. Control Bus and Modulation Visibility: The Control Bus tab now surfaces Control Bus Mixes as sources alongside individual buses, and the Modulation tab filters down to only active control bus columns to reduce noise. Live Monitoring: Audio Insights can now display trace data in real-time without saving a trace file, eliminating disk space concerns during long monitoring sessions. Both editor and standalone versions (via Unreal Insights) are supported. Event Log: A new dockable Events tab provides a live, scrollable chronological log of sound start, stop, and other audio events. Events are text-filterable, time-selectable to sync other visualizations, and double-clickable to navigate directly to the corresponding instance in the Sounds tab. Plots: A dedicated Plots tab consolidates per-sound parameter plotting with improved rendering, corrected color continuity across trace pauses, and fixed display artifacts in standalone. Standalone and Cache Improvements: The data cache manager now works in standalone sessions, trace data can be saved to a file directly from dashboard caches, and the cache size is now user-configurable via settings. For more information on this feature, see Audio Insights.
title: Unreal Engine 5.8 Release Notes

text: Plots: A dedicated Plots tab consolidates per-sound parameter plotting with improved rendering, corrected color continuity across trace pauses, and fixed display artifacts in standalone. Standalone and Cache Improvements: The data cache manager now works in standalone sessions, trace data can be saved to a file directly from dashboard caches, and the cache size is now user-configurable via settings. For more information on this feature, see Audio Insights. Audio subtitles are required for accessibility – dialogue systems, closed captioning, and voice chat. We promoted the plugin from Experimental to Beta status, reflecting its increased stability and feature completeness. Subtitles now display correctly for all sound types triggered within a MetaSound graph, including nested MetaSounds. Per-platform subtitle display overrides are now supported, allowing different widget placement and styling for platforms such as mobile or Nintendo Switch where screen layout differs. Subtitles in a Level Sequence can now be previewed directly in the editor without entering Play In Editor (PIE), making iteration on subtitle timing faster. Subtitle duration can now be overridden per locale, automatically using the duration of the locale-specific sound wave when a localized asset is present. A new QueueSingleSubtitle Blueprint and C++ function replaces the older QueueSubtitle (now deprecated). A companion function, QueueSubtitlesFromAsset, queues all subtitle lines stored in an asset in a single call with correct timing offsets applied automatically. We added a Comment field to subtitle assets for internal notes visible in the editor but not shown at runtime. Sound designers need powerful editing tools without leaving the engine. We are continuing to improve the Waveform Editor with deeper control over fades and workflow refinements to reduce round-trips to external audio tools. Fades are now decoupled from trim. A new Fade transformation allows any number of independent fade regions — each with their own fade-in and fade-out — to be placed anywhere on the waveform, completely independent of the TrimFade region. Trim fade-in and fade-out curve types can also now be set directly from the toolbar, with right-click context menus on fade handles providing additional curve shape options. Scrolling on a fade handle adjusts the curve slope.
title: Unreal Engine 5.8 Release Notes

text: A new Fade transformation allows any number of independent fade regions — each with their own fade-in and fade-out — to be placed anywhere on the waveform, completely independent of the TrimFade region. Trim fade-in and fade-out curve types can also now be set directly from the toolbar, with right-click context menus on fade handles providing additional curve shape options. Scrolling on a fade handle adjusts the curve slope. Reimport is now available from the editor toolbar, with three modes: reimport and overwrite transformations (including marker and loop region data from cue and smpl chunks), reimport keeping existing transformations, or reimport from a new file entirely. A new Launch Transformations setting helps you pre-configure which transformations are automatically applied when opening a SoundWave that has none. This removes repetitive setup steps for standard editing workflows. When transformation changes are applied, the SoundWave's LUFS and Sample Peak metadata now update automatically to reflect the transformed waveform, keeping asset metadata accurate without requiring a manual refresh. G skips the playhead to the next marker. H snaps the playhead to the nearest zero crossing. Enter stops playback and rewinds to the start. Shift+Space resets the playhead to the beginning of the file without affecting playback state. To get started with this feature, see Waveform Editor Quick Start. MetaSound Node Configuration, introduced in UE 5.7, is now expanded in UE 5.8 with new tools that reduce boilerplate for developers and improve the editing experience for designers. Dynamic Interface Node Configuration: A new built-in FMetaSoundDynamicInterfaceNodeConfiguration struct automatically manages sub-interface instance counts and variant type selection based on a node's FClassInterface definition. Developers no longer need to write custom per-node configuration structs for the common case of exposing sub-interface counts or variant pin types — the Details panel now surfaces these controls automatically as dropdowns and count fields. Node Update Transform API: A new, more structured API for authoring node update scripts gives developers fine-grained control over how nodes migrate when their interface changes across major versions. Custom update logic is now associated with a specific major version and runs after minor-version and interface updates have been applied, ensuring predictable ordering.
title: Unreal Engine 5.8 Release Notes

text: Node Update Transform API: A new, more structured API for authoring node update scripts gives developers fine-grained control over how nodes migrate when their interface changes across major versions. Custom update logic is now associated with a specific major version and runs after minor-version and interface updates have been applied, ensuring predictable ordering. An example migration — updating the biquad filter's default bandwidth from 1.0 to 2.0 for newly-placed nodes while preserving the legacy default for existing content — demonstrates the pattern. Sub-Interface Layout Serialization: Sub-interface layout information is now correctly reconstituted when deserializing MetaSounds, resolving cases where vertex name collisions and layout loss occurred on certain platforms. API Stability: FClassInterface exits its experimental designation in UE 5.8. FNodeClassMetadata::DefaultInterface now accepts FClassInterface directly (replacing FVertexInterface), and deprecated input/output node creation helpers have been removed from IDataTypeRegistry. Developers building Node Configuration integrations can treat this as the stable public API surface going forward. MetaSound Templates is a new Experimental feature in UE 5.8 that gives audio programmers the means to create reusable, property-driven MetaSound generation logic that sound designers can use enabling rapid iteration without ever having to touch the graph. A Template is a C++ defined UStruct that can procedurally configure and rebuild a MetaSound graph, its interface, and inputs any time a designer changes one of its exposed properties. Templates can limit what Designers see to only the properties the template author chose to expose; the underlying graph, member list, page options, and more, can optionally be hidden entirely. The programmer defines a small set of parameters they want designers to control — a list of sounds, a pitch range, a filter cutoff — and the Template's code handles configuring the given options into a valid MetaSound graph. From the MetaSound Editor, designers select a template from the new Template toolbar dropdown and edit its properties in the MetaSound Details panel. Converting a templated MetaSound back to a standard one (preserving the last generated graph state) is also supported. A template can also ship a fully custom UMG widget tab built on Unreal's MVVM framework, providing a purpose-built interface — sliders, previews, array editors — instead of or alongside the default MetaSound panels. A Randomizer template ships with UE 5.8 as a reference implementation.
title: Unreal Engine 5.8 Release Notes

text: Converting a templated MetaSound back to a standard one (preserving the last generated graph state) is also supported. A template can also ship a fully custom UMG widget tab built on Unreal's MVVM framework, providing a purpose-built interface — sliders, previews, array editors — instead of or alongside the default MetaSound panels. A Randomizer template ships with UE 5.8 as a reference implementation. It picks randomly from a designer-specified list of Sound Waves, applies a pitch offset within a configurable semitone range, and supports both one-shot and looping playback modes. It is hidden by default in UE 5.8, but serves as a working code example for template authors. Full Pipeline Integration: CAT output is now wired through MetaSoundSource meaning a MetaSound graph can produce a CAT signal and deliver it directly to the audio engine. The channel format can be automatically determined by looking at the sound waves set on the MetaSoundSource inputs. Data-Defined Audio Formats: Custom channel configurations can now be declared as first-class audio formats and used directly within graphs. This enables teams to define and work with non-standard or proprietary speaker layouts without forking engine code. Ambisonics and Transcoding: First-order Ambisonics is now a built-in CAT format. Transcoding between Discrete and Ambisonics formats is handled automatically at graph boundaries, so spatial audio workflows no longer require manual conversion nodes. Wave Player 2.0: A next-generation wave player reimplemented on top of the CAT foundation utilizing experimental sound asset container. CAT Mixer: A dedicated mixing node for combining multichannel CAT signals within a graph Grain Player: A grain synthesis playback node built on the CAT pipeline Multiply: The Multiply node gains new CAT-aware variants: Multichannel signals can now be scaled and modulated without collapsing to mono first, enabling per-channel gain, ring modulation, and envelope shaping directly on multichannel buses. Ladder Filter: We ported the Ladder Filter to process both standard AudioBuffer and CAT signals. The existing mono filter path is preserved; the CAT path handles multichannel audio with independent per-channel filtering. This conversion also serves as the reference implementation for porting additional MetaSound DSP nodes to CAT. Sound designers using Sequencer for cinematics, gameplay sequences, and rendering frequently hit friction around audio mixing control, default behaviors that don't match expectations, and audio quality issues in exported renders.
title: Unreal Engine 5.8 Release Notes

text: The existing mono filter path is preserved; the CAT path handles multichannel audio with independent per-channel filtering. This conversion also serves as the reference implementation for porting additional MetaSound DSP nodes to CAT. Sound designers using Sequencer for cinematics, gameplay sequences, and rendering frequently hit friction around audio mixing control, default behaviors that don't match expectations, and audio quality issues in exported renders. In UE 5.8 we are shipping a significant set of improvements across three areas. Two new Sequencer tracks bring Audio Modulation directly into the timeline. The Control Bus Track makes it possible for any Audio Modulation Control Bus — volume, pitch, filter cutoff, or any custom modulation parameter — to be keyframed and animated over time within a sequence. The Control Bus Mix Track provides a way to activate and deactivate a pre-defined Control Bus Mix (a set of modulation values applied together) at specific points in the sequence, enabling precise and repeatable audio mix states tied to cinematic events. We redefined Audio section looping behavior to align more closely with typical sound designer intent; users define if a sound will play to completion rather than reusing concepts of KeepState or RestoreState when the section is finished, and Looping was renamed as Repeating to distinguish between section on game frame boundaries and asset looping on sample boundaries. Audio sections no longer auto-expand when keyframes are added outside their bounds. MetaSound integration enables more reliable playback of MetaSound sources. The audio evaluation system has been improved to avoid unnecessary stop-and-restart when the playhead context jumps, resulting in smoother scrubbing and pause/resume behavior. MRQ now supports expanded submix selection for audio export, giving you direct control over which submix is recorded rather than being limited to the default output. We fixed audio popping, gaps, and repeats that previously occurred at camera cut boundaries; the audio component is now paused and resumed across cuts rather than stopped and restarted, eliminating sample-level discontinuities in rendered output. In Unreal Engine 5.8, we switched the default audio backend on Windows from XAudio2 to WASAPI. The new AudioMixerWasapi module is now selected automatically; XAudio2 remains available as an opt-in fallback. The same backend is also used on Xbox. No changes are required on the developers end.
title: Unreal Engine 5.8 Release Notes

text: In Unreal Engine 5.8, we switched the default audio backend on Windows from XAudio2 to WASAPI. The new AudioMixerWasapi module is now selected automatically; XAudio2 remains available as an opt-in fallback. The same backend is also used on Xbox. No changes are required on the developers end. All content should behave the same — only the layer that talks to the operating system has changed. Future-proofing. Building on a supported, actively-maintained Windows API instead of a legacy one. Better latency capabilities. Direct access to the lower-level API gives the audio mixer more control over buffer scheduling. More robust device handling. The WASAPI backend now includes full device-swap support — plugging or unplugging headphones, switching the Windows default device, or having audio drivers force a device change is handled cleanly by the engine. Quality and reliability improvements. Over the course of the 5.8 cycle, the audio team hardened the backend against a long list of real-world device-change, format-negotiation, and shutdown edge cases discovered in production. The result is a more stable Windows audio path out of the box. This is a Module, not a plugin. WASAPI ships as the AudioMixerWasapi module inside the engine. There's nothing to enable or install. Device swap is supported. Headset connect/disconnect, default-device changes, and sample-rate changes are all handled by the backend. Opting out (fallback to XAudio2). If you hit a project-specific issue, you can revert to the previous backend by adding the following to your project's Config/Windows/WindowsEngine.ini: We recommend reporting any issue you encounter so it can be addressed before XAudio2 is eventually removed. With Unreal Engine 5.8, we advance the mobile renderer and expand access to higher-quality rendering features on supported devices. Multi-pass deferred rendering as the default path across mobile platforms (with forward rendering still available as an opt-in). Mobile support for SSAO, SSR, deferred decals, contact shadows, and higher-quality water rendering. In UE 5.8 we also introduce half-precision (FP16) shader usage in targeted materials and global shader passes, improving performance while preserving visual quality. Together, these changes raise visual fidelity and scalability on high-end mobile hardware while preserving performance and giving teams more headroom to tune quality levels. With Unreal Engine 5.8, we deliver targeted Android platform improvements focused on input support and iteration speed.
title: Unreal Engine 5.8 Release Notes

text: In UE 5.8 we also introduce half-precision (FP16) shader usage in targeted materials and global shader passes, improving performance while preserving visual quality. Together, these changes raise visual fidelity and scalability on high-end mobile hardware while preserving performance and giving teams more headroom to tune quality levels. With Unreal Engine 5.8, we deliver targeted Android platform improvements focused on input support and iteration speed. Simpler automated setup of developer workstations using Turnkey. These changes improve developer productivity and platform robustness for teams building and testing Android projects. In Unreal Engine 5.8, we improve the visual fidelity of the Preview Platform feature so visuals displayed in the Editor more closely match the look and behavior of target hardware. Together with Valve we have implemented experimental support for their next XR platform: bPackageForOpenXRImmersive is a new setting that defaults to true in the VR Template. In UE 5.8, OpenXR stereo layers can now be drawn behind the main scene. This opens up XR effects that used to require engine modifications or vendor-specific plugins. Before UE 5.8, Unreal Engine's OpenXR support always drew stereo layers on top of the projection layer (the rendered UE world), and face-locked layers always sat above world-locked ones. That fixed order made true "underlays" — layers that appear behind the environment — impossible out of the box, even though the OpenXR spec itself just takes an ordered list of layers with no such rule. This change replaces the fixed order with one driven by layer priority, matching how OpenXR works. It adds two new settings: xr.OpenXRProjectionLayerPriority (default = 0). The priority of the projection layer. Any stereo layer with a lower priority is drawn behind it; anything higher is drawn in front, as before. xr.OpenXRSortFaceLockedLayersAboveOtherLayers (off by default) — when on, face-locked layers always draw above everything else, regardless of priority.
title: Unreal Engine 5.8 Release Notes

text: This change replaces the fixed order with one driven by layer priority, matching how OpenXR works. It adds two new settings: xr.OpenXRProjectionLayerPriority (default = 0). The priority of the projection layer. Any stereo layer with a lower priority is drawn behind it; anything higher is drawn in front, as before. xr.OpenXRSortFaceLockedLayersAboveOtherLayers (off by default) — when on, face-locked layers always draw above everything else, regardless of priority. This matches the old behavior. To restore the pre-UE 5.8 order, set xr.OpenXRSortFaceLockedLayersAboveOtherLayers=1 and set xr.OpenXRProjectionLayerPriority to a value lower than every stereo layer priority in your project (for example, -2147483648, the minimum 32-bit integer). text: With Unreal Engine 5.8, we introduce a new Editor Gizmo System designed to deliver a more consistent and flexible interaction experience across the editor. Built on top of the Interactive Tools Framework, the new system consolidates multiple legacy gizmo implementations into a single framework used across viewports and tools. The redesigned gizmos also include a range of visual and usability improvements inspired by workflows familiar to artists and level designers from tools like Maya and Blender. With improved hit targets, clearer visual feedback, customizable interaction presets, and enhanced precision controls, the new system provides a faster and more predictable workflow for manipulating actors and assets. Improved Scaling Behavior: Gizmos now operate more reliably from all viewing angles, enabling more predictable scaling interactions. Numeric Delta Overlays: Real-time overlays display movement, rotation, or scale deltas during interaction. Delta Line Indicators: Visual lines indicate how far an object has been translated from its original position. Rotation Delta Line: Rotation interactions display a visual delta line similar to Blender, improving precision when rotating from greater distances. Customizable Gizmo Behavior: Increased flexibility for teams to configure interactions based on their preferred workflow. Precision Mode: Temporarily slow down transformations for fine adjustments. Nudge Mode: Incrementally adjust translation, rotation, or scale for controlled edits. With an eye toward post-compositing workflows, the Light Modifier enables artists to set and override property values for light actors on a per-render layer basis in Movie Render Graph. Using the same level and level sequence, artists can isolate individual lights or groups of lights and render shots with different values for intensity, color, and/or any custom property on any type of light. Properties can also be made into graph variables and exposed as overrides in both the Quick Render and the Movie Render Queue windows. Real-time performance considerations for depth of field rendering can limit visual quality on shots that emphasize it in their design. In order to achieve more “filmic” depth of field, artists must move to the Path Tracer, which has a higher cost in rendering time, and do so for all shots for consistency, even the ones that don’t rely on depth of field. Ideally, there could be an option to have the best of both worlds in terms of performance and quality. Accumulation Depth of Field is a new feature that renders depth of field by accumulating deferred renders from multiple aperture view points using Movie Render Graph. This greatly mitigates artifacts due to missing parallax while preserving deferred rendering look development. Artists can use it when they don’t get the desired visual results with the default depth of field and avoid the cost on shots that don’t need it. Dataflow is Unreal Engine’s node-based system for procedural generation of physics-based assets. It’s widely used in workflows for Cloth, Destruction, Hair, Flesh, and MetaHuman setups. UE 5.8 updates include: Enhanced UI and UX (more interactive tooling, gizmos, and more). The Chaos Visual Debugger (CVD) provides Unreal Engine users with a way to effectively observe and debug their physics simulations, either directly in the Unreal Editor or from a standalone CVD instance. UE 5.8 updates include: We are adding foundational improvements to Unreal Engine’s Chaos physics system to support more responsive and scalable simulation workflows. UE 5.8 updates include: More control over object sensitivity and island sleeping. Better intra-island parallelisation via spatial or color separation. A protected solver API and new execution model. Continued work to remove the monolithic physics thread and move to the job graph. Better scale and clamping within the rigid body and deformable solvers.
title: Unreal Engine 5.8 Release Notes

text: UE 5.8 updates include: More control over object sensitivity and island sleeping. Better intra-island parallelisation via spatial or color separation. A protected solver API and new execution model. Continued work to remove the monolithic physics thread and move to the job graph. Better scale and clamping within the rigid body and deformable solvers. Chaos++ solver node for Dataflow use, to prove out early API external to the world solver. The Caching framework project focuses on extending the existing system for storing and replaying simulation data efficiently across Chaos-based features like Cloth, Fluids, Destruction, and Flesh. UE 5.8 updates include: Using the Chaos cache asset as a meta-asset pointing to more relevant optimized formats. Added tools for cache versioning, trimming, and invalidation. Expanded support for painting attributes, skin weighting, and guide swapping. Flesh nodes take advantage of the new Dataflow rendering system. With UE 5.8, Chaos cloth is production ready. Updates include: Enabled non-destructive updates and round-trip editing with CLO/Marvelous Designer. Import USD constraints and cloth attributes into Unreal Engine. Enabled procedural interactions between layers (skin, muscle, garment). Improved performance through shared memory and solver logic. Cloth Interactor asset data to help manage setting groups of properties from Blueprints. Added fictitious forces on full velocity scale simulations. The Modular Vehicle system gives users the ability to build vehicles in real time using dynamic scene graph components rather than relying on fixed skeletal meshes. Designed with client-predicted and server-authoritative physics, it supports flexible construction. This system empowers creators to craft traditional or unconventional vehicles using modular parts within Unreal Engine. Added support for constructing vehicles using a skeletal mesh, giving users a way to easily create simple vehicles with the same framework. Added two-way interaction between the vehicle and the ground. For more information on this feature, see Chaos Modular Vehicles. text: Added URootMotionModifier_Blueprintable, new MotionWarping URootMotionModifier blue print overridable. PoseSearchDatabase fix for not being able to copy paste in an empty database. PoseSearchDatabase DDC key generation fix, to support objects with duplicated down dependencies. Fixed a bug where for inconsistent past velocities in motion matching due to history points being offset by delta time, causing noise in past velocity when delta time is not constant. Fixed PoseSearchDatabase editor preview of static mesh attachments. Fixed crash in FAsyncPoseSearchDatabasesManagement::RequestAsyncBuildIndex when database dependent animation assets failed to compress. Fix for missing PoseSearchDatabase indexing on reverting and reloading dependent assets. Fix for missing FMemMark(s) in FPoseSearchColumn::Filter and FPoseSearchColumn::SetOutputs. Fix for PoseSearchDatabase DDC key determinism when supporting Choosers PoseSearchColumns. Making sure there're no flying animation tasks when on game thread by calling GetProxyOnAnyThread, so it's safe to access animinstance variables in UPoseSearchLibrary::MotionMatch. Fix for UPoseSearchLibrary::MotionMatch crashing when reusing an invalid continuing pose from a previously evaluated schema. Add an "AdditionalRotationOffset" in the root motion modifier that allows rotational offset to be specified per animation. This avoids conflicting rotations when warp points are used by multiple different actions. Note that any setup using a rotational offset with facing mode will need to be manually adjusted (this was introduced in 5.7). Deprecated EMotionWarpRotationType::OppositeFacing and EMotionWarpRotationType::OppositeDefault since they can be achieved with an additional rotational offset of 180 degrees (existing data will be automatically converted). Stop using the warp point's rotation offset when in facing mode. Fix for crash while changing levels because of invalid FRewindDebuggerTrajectory::WorldToVisualize. Fix to allow the DisplayWorldId to be set while analyzing local sessions. Without this, the debugged mesh is lost after the PIE session ends. Fix montages do not mark blending out sources as inactive. Fix for previewing game generated pose search debugger data with the editor. Fix for SearchThrottleTime not working properly in FAnimNode_MotionMatching::UpdateAssetPlayer and FMotionMatchingTrait::PreUpdate. Fix for crash in USkeletalMeshComponent::ForEachBodyBelow when instantiated Bodies do not match the SkeletalBodySetups in the Reference Skeleton Mesh. Fix for FAssetIndexer::Process crashing on schemas with roles improperly setup. Fix issue where GetPoseIndex could return an invalid pose index when there are multiple sampling ranges on the same animation asset. Deprecated: UPoseSearchFeatureChannel_Curve::BP_GetCurveValue, UPoseSearchFeatureChannel_Heading::BP_GetWorldRotation, UPoseSearchFeatureChannel_Velocity::BP_GetWorldVelocity, UPoseSearchFeatureChannel_Position::BP_GetWorldPosition, in favor of UPoseSearchFeatureChannel_Curve::BP_GetCurveValueFromContext, UPoseSearchFeatureChannel_Heading::BP_GetWorldRotationFromContext, UPoseSearchFeatureChannel_Velocity::BP_GetWorldVelocityFromContext, UPoseSearchFeatureChannel_Position::BP_GetWorldPositionFromContext, taking the more versatile FChooserEvaluationContext as input.

Override Set editor: Add Child, Search Bar, Keyboard Shortcuts, Duplicate, Reordering Added DuplicateRetargetOverrideSet() to the controller API (Blueprint/Python callable). Creates a new override set with a unique name, copying all property overrides, parent assignment, and active-by-default state from the source set. Added "Duplicate" entry to the Override Set tree view context menu between Rename and Unparent. Add Child: Context menu action to create a new override set parented under the selected set. Added bRetainAdditiveFlags to FIKRetargetBatchOperationInputs so that Blueprint and Python scripts can control whether additive animation attributes are preserved during batch retarget. Updated all 17 biped templates to split the existing LeftLeg/RightLeg chains: LeftLeg/RightLeg chains now end at the ankle/foot bone (previously ended at ball/toe) New LeftFoot/RightFoot chains cover the ball/toe bone. IK goals remain on the leg chains, now created at the ankle/foot bone. Added new Templates for Blender Rigify and Meshcapade. Add override set dropdown to Batch Retarget window When using a manually supplied IK Retargeter in the Batch/Auto Retarget window, there was no way to select override sets. Added a dropdown (FName with GetOptions) that lists available override sets from the assigned retargeter asset. text: Added a dropdown (FName with GetOptions) that lists available override sets from the assigned retargeter asset. Selected override set is applied to both the live preview viewport and animation export. Dropdown is disabled when using auto-generated retargeter. Improved RigMapper Definition editor graph Comment nodes to fully enclose selected nodes and to trigger on "C" key command. Improved validation messages and notifications for RigMapper Definition editor graph. Notifications are now displayed in the graph header. Before they could be seen only in log. Added Math Operations feature to RigMapper Definition with a corresponding node in RigMapper Definition editor graph. This op includes all unary, binary and N-array standard mathematical operations selected through the drop down box. Improved zooming in/focusing a node and all connected nodes by lowering opacity to non selected nodes and zooming in/out to capture selected ones. Implemented Comment node feature for RigMapper Definition graph. RigMapper refactoring to include numerous quality of life changes: Persistent node positions between sessions (Graph is no longer recreated every time it is opened). Added feature which imports Input curves from Skeletal Mesh. Fixed a problem with RigMapper Definition cache not being cleared when modified. RigMapper Op is now a sub-operation of CurveRemap Op. RigMapper divided into RetargetRigMapperUserDataOp which uses RigMapper Definition embedded in target mesh UserData, and RetargetRigMapperOp which contains single RigMapper Definition data asset. Added possibility to select multiple RigMapper Ops in a single substack. Added support for breaking links from a node. Added support for moving links from one node to another. Implemented support for adding new connections by dragging and dropping to a different node. IK Rig: Allow enabling/disabling anim graph node w/ cvar a.animnode.IKRig.Enable. Allowed adding more pins to nodes and automatically generating connections to other nodes. Fixed a bug with importing a Definition from JSON file. Added constraints when removing pins so the minimal required number of pins are preserved depending on the feature. Nodes can be moved around, although position will not pre preserved on reopening. Nodes can be created from a connection or standalone though a context menu. Nodes can be updated through details panel on the right side.
title: Unreal Engine 5.8 Release Notes

text: Fixed a bug with importing a Definition from JSON file. Added constraints when removing pins so the minimal required number of pins are preserved depending on the feature. Nodes can be moved around, although position will not pre preserved on reopening. Nodes can be created from a connection or standalone though a context menu. Nodes can be updated through details panel on the right side. Added a Context menu on right click on node or graph. Nodes can be relinked and links can be removed. Fixed and improved RigMapper Linked Definition validation to include NullOutputs which are subsequently used as inputs. Relaxed validation of hanging inputs and outputs for RigMapper Linked and Baked Definitions to allow pass-through with a warning. RigMapper definitions tongue fix on RM_CDH_FNM, RM_MHH_CDH and related Linked Definitions and Baked definitions. Updated RM_CDH_FNM rig definition to address an issue with inverted corner sharpen and upper eyelid controls. Cleaned deprecated methods from MLDeformer (up to 5.6). Add BP support for specifying collision ignore/include pairs - Enable/DisableCollisionBetweenBodies. Enable/disable angular drives applies to slerp as well as twist/swing. Make sure that limb-generated controls get automatically added to a set with the limb name. Fixes for Physics Control Component names, so they're never called "". Note that this will change the names of some controls/modifiers, and if those are being referenced explicitly (by name) the assets will need to be patched up. Adds checks that controls/modifiers/sets that are passed in are valid (and optionally warns if not). Drives now have a Join Limit Violation Response. The available options are: Clamp the skeletal animation drive targets to joint limits, or Widen limits to accommodate the target. In addition to either respecting the joint's limit or the animation, this prevents spurious forces and torques present when drive and limits are fighting (response 'None' option). PhysicsControl plugin is now marked as ready for production use. Support for applying forces in the control rig physics and RigidBodyWithControl animation graph nodes. Physics Control Component: Addresses various problems with tick ordering/dependencies so that 1. it waits until the input pose is ready and 2. it ensures the tick is not pushed into PostPhysics by (for example) CharacterMovementComponent when on dynamic floors.
title: Unreal Engine 5.8 Release Notes

text: PhysicsControl plugin is now marked as ready for production use. Support for applying forces in the control rig physics and RigidBodyWithControl animation graph nodes. Physics Control Component: Addresses various problems with tick ordering/dependencies so that 1. it waits until the input pose is ready and 2. it ensures the tick is not pushed into PostPhysics by (for example) CharacterMovementComponent when on dynamic floors. Turned off by default. Added guarding against negative blend times on montages. Added CVar a.Montage.UseForcedFromPositionAsSubStepOrigin - if ForcedNextFromPosition is set, use it as the sub-stepping origin in FAnimMontageInstance::Advance instead of the previous internal position. Enabled by default. Added the option to display trajectory velocity in debug log. Add FPoseValueBundle as a typed pose overlay for FValueBundle. Implicit cross-skeleton remapping at graph input boundary. Remaps poses automatically when a foreign skeleton enters a graph via PushPose so node authors never deal with cross-skeleton concerns. Add the ability in UAF to specify the end tick group for events. Add package path to some rigvm compile error reports. Add CharacterMovementComponent to allowed class types in RigVM. Add CVar to suppress duplicate anim node slot names warning. Add CVar that allows for using MovieScene GUID rather than channel hashing for partial-UAnimSequencerDataModel hash (significant speed-up, downside is MovieScene GUID invalidation is non-deterministic). Added additional pose validity checks when getting the target transform of a bone socket references. Added additional pose validity checks to ConvertWidgetLocation in FAnimNodeEditMode. Reimplementation of "Speed up UAnimSequence::CreateDerivedDataKeyHash" - drastically decreases time spend on Animation Sequence its DDC key generation. Expose certain solver collision settings to RBAN and RBWC nodes to allow for improved environmental collisions. This gives parity with functionality in control rig physics. Also added a new category for the details panels to clean up the UI. Added Scoped Crash Data For Animations (Make animation crashes easy to debug).
title: Unreal Engine 5.8 Release Notes

Notify States: Added the option to not merge the lifetime of notify states on concurrent plays of the same animation asset. This doesn't prevent the notifies from being sampled but the associated events will not be dispatched at the end of animation update when the flag is set. Allow priority to be set on transitions to conduits so it's possible to deprioritize them vs transitions to other states. Force property access pre-event graph update callsite to be invoked prior to InitializeRootNode being called. This prevents property access errors coming from anim nodes that call GetEvaluateGraphExposedInputs from Initialize_AnyThread. Added standard blend for Anim Graph mirroring node. Add user-exposed NotifyInstanceID to FAnimNotifyEventReference. This can be used in user events to tell notify instances apart. Added populating the error log with names of missing skeleton bones, when a mesh has bones that do not exist in the skeleton yet. Removed no longer used additive total bone weight array from the BlendProfileScratchData and SlotEvaluatePoseWithBlendProfiles. Add 'Ignore Pose Asset Source Animation Curves' property to the pose blend node. Marked UAnimInstance::GetCurrentStateName as const and added const correctness in function body. Add filter for non-additive animations in the animation editor asset browser. Removed deprecated functions in USkeleton (GetSkeletonRemapping, GetAssetRegistryTags, CollectAnimationNotifies, GetRawAnimationTrackIndex). Fixed uninitialized variable ContentOnly in SRigVMFunctionPicker causing state tree function binding regression. Fix: ExecuteBindings_GT not gated by external prereqs added via module dependency traits. Fix for multiple copies of variable instances showing up in rewind debugger for graphs. Fix for GetHostTransform not reporting the correct value until the actor has moved after spawn. Add handling for rare cases where anim sequence memory mapping fails.

Fix for crash in Constraint AnimNode when changing setup while running. text: Avoid crashing when blend space sample uses a null animation sequence. Always preload animation sequence dependencies as MT async loading requires manual handling. Fixed crash when updating blend samples in a Blendspace while PIE is running in a separate window. Fixed crashes caused by NaN bone transforms coming from AnimNode_StrideWarping. Fix for potential NaN bone transforms generated inside AnimNode_FootPlacement if root is rotated exactly 90 degrees from expected approach direction. Set anim group follower LeaderScore to always be less than any possible leader, to avoid selecting any follower as leader if there's any leader in the FAnimGroupInstance. Skeletal mesh component now refreshes the skeletal mesh asset at PostEditImport, so the skeletal mesh is not lost after a duplicate. Fixed crash in DebugDrawSkeleton when using 'show bones' command. Make SharedContext a unique ptr to force destruction when released in FAnimNode_SaveCachedPose::PostGraphUpdate. Fix potential thread-unsafe access to skeleton remapping data. In that case of FReferenceSkeleton, limit when the remapping data is refreshed to only when it's a skeleton and not a mesh that is having it's ref skeleton rebuilt. Fix issue with blended curve container not correctly tracking when it is sorted. Fix to allow notifies that are sampled via AnimSingleNodeInstance to store the current playback time. This means that UAnimNotifyLibrary functions that rely on the current time can be used on these notifies. Enable FBoneSocket Target Pickers in Contexts Outside Anim Montages. Cleaned deprecated methods from animation runtime (up to 5.6). Removed non-reflected UE_DEPRECATED items (5.0-5.6) spanning Engine/Source/Runtime/Engine/{Classes, Public}/Animation, Engine/Source/Runtime/AnimGraphRuntime (+ MovieSceneTracks anim nodes), and Engine/Source/Editor/AnimGraph compiler interfaces. title: Unreal Engine 5.8 Release Notes

text: Cleaned deprecated methods from LiveLink (up to 5.6). UAF: Fixed incorrect deprecation logic in AnimNextComponent when loading Blueprints with data inheritance on deprecated variables. Delete Mark is now Delete Selected Marks which allows the selected marks to be deleted at once. Add Mark is now Add Mark at Playhead which adds a mark at the current playhead as opposed to where the mouse was pressed. Playing a sequence in the editor now honors the time bounds (selection range when set, otherwise playback range), matching rewind and key-jump behavior. Playhead scrubbing can now be limited to the selection range, in addition to None and Playback Range. Bake Transform is now available from the object binding right-click menu. Added missing Convert to Spawnable command binding, and route Level Sequence conversions through Convert To Custom Binding so custom-binding spawnables work. Bake Transform now disables the original track instead of toggling each section, matching the Bake to Control Rig behavior. Add support for Material Slots Overlay Material switching and parameter animation. . Assigning a spawnable to an object property now creates an Actor Reference Track automatically, so the reference doesn't go stale when the spawnable's path changes. Component Attachment tracks now respect hierarchical bias, so a higher‑priority attachment section correctly overrides a lower‑priority one when they overlap. The Actor Reference track now supports Completion Mode, so disabling or muting them properly restores the prior reference. Jump to Next/Previous Key now respects looping. When looping is off, it no longer wraps past the first/last key. Add Selection from Content Browser is now a bindable command, so you can assign it a keyboard shortcut in editor preferences. The Actor Reference track (used for properties like the Cine Camera's Look At Target) has been upgraded to Sequencer's ECS evaluation system, aligning its performance and ordering with other tracks. Lighting channels on primitive components are now animatable. Dragging a marked frame now translates selected keys and sections along with it. Pausing the game now pauses the Sequencer clock as well (opt out via Sequencer.AllowPausedClock 0). The back/forward mouse buttons now navigate forwards/backwards through sequences, matching the Blueprint editor's tab navigation. Snap to Markers while scrubbing now snap to the playback start/end and selection start/end frames.
title: Unreal Engine 5.8 Release Notes

text: Lighting channels on primitive components are now animatable. Dragging a marked frame now translates selected keys and sections along with it. Pausing the game now pauses the Sequencer clock as well (opt out via Sequencer.AllowPausedClock 0). The back/forward mouse buttons now navigate forwards/backwards through sequences, matching the Blueprint editor's tab navigation. Snap to Markers while scrubbing now snap to the playback start/end and selection start/end frames. Markers are now also selected with Select All in Selection Range, Select Forwards, and Select Backwards. Added a new option to Select Markers in Selection Range. The Add Track button for Subsequences now allows creation of custom Level Sequence subclasses. Remove DisplayName="Anim Sequence" for MovieSceneSkeletalAnimationSection because it conflicts with Anim Sequence assets. Add a way for stitch track to work with Animation Blueprints. This is a bit of a workaround for the issue of pose history not being able to be both read from and written to easily via an attribute, which is necessary for the stitch track. Now, the user can add an 'OverridePoseHistoryName' which, in animation Blueprint mode, will look for a pose history node tagged with that name and pull the pose history from it for use in the stitch track. This allows the pose history node to be _after_ the sequencer target node, which is necessary for blending out to work correctly. In addition, we set up an example properly in the AnimSandbox to show this working. Deselect marked frames when keys and sections are also deselected. Disallow marked frame movement when they are locked. Limit Viewport Selection is now in the viewport menu whenever a sequence is active (was Animation-Mode-only); UMG and Actor Sequence get the button in their own toolbar. Anim In Engine: Control Rig use ECS evaluation by default Users can fall back to legacy evaluation with: ControlRig.UseLegacySequencerTemplate true. Add SequencerTools toolset for AI-driven sequence creation and editing. Added call to Global Dependency Graph update cache in OnAllModuleLoadingPhasesComplete to prevent the graph's cache to update when the first sequence is played. In the event that a plugin/module that mutates this graph loads after OnAllModuleLoadingPhasesComplete, the cache will be invalidated and will be updated when the first sequence is played. Sequence Validator: Fixed Whole Section Ranges rule reporting incorrect results.

text: Add SequencerTools toolset for AI-driven sequence creation and editing. Added call to Global Dependency Graph update cache in OnAllModuleLoadingPhasesComplete to prevent the graph's cache to update when the first sequence is played. In the event that a plugin/module that mutates this graph loads after OnAllModuleLoadingPhasesComplete, the cache will be invalidated and will be updated when the first sequence is played. Sequence Validator: Fixed Whole Section Ranges rule reporting incorrect results. Visibility Track keys are now correctly set with their current values. Visibility is inverted from their Hidden property and the setting of the key was not correctly inverted. Fix FVector2f/3f/4f tracks dropping keys silently UnpackChannelsFromOperational(const FFloatIntermediateVectorand) was writing FMovieSceneDoubleChannel entries, but UMovieSceneFloatVectorSection stores FMovieSceneFloatChannel curves. When keying, the channel proxy lookup returned nullptr and the key was silently dropped. Cooking a project that uses Time Warp tracks inside child Level Sequences no longer fails with an "illegal reference to private object" error. The camera cut tracks which have preroll now take into account the instance transform data of a level sequence which is passed to the streaming manager. Update the possessed object class when matching possessable GUIDs (including ones that bind to spawnables), so bindings no longer hold a stale class. Conditional sections inside a subsequence now evaluate correctly when a parent sequence is conditionally disabled. Sequences with camera rig rails are no longer incorrectly marked dirty on save. Spline components in these camera rig rails are just visualization components, and those don't need to be regenerated or have their physics state be recreated on save. Fixed a RepLayout mismatch from an editor-only field in MovieSceneSequencePlaybackSettings. The entity system threading model is now refreshed at each call site after ScheduleTasks, instead of inside ExecutePhase where it was computed too early. Fix race condition in TEntityTaskComponents::Schedule_PerAllocation Schedule_PerAllocation on TEntityTaskComponents (the unfiltered path) was setting bSerialTasks = false, making it behave identically to Fork_PerAllocation and allowing multiple allocations to run in parallel on different threads. This violated the Schedule_ contract that guarantees serial execution of ForEachAllocation calls. The filtered variant (TFilteredEntityTask::Schedule_PerAllocation) and both Schedule_PerEntity overloads correctly set bSerialTasks = true. Film overlay options menu commands no longer stop working because they were bound to a transient widget that could be destroyed when the toolbar refreshed.

title: Unreal Engine 5.8 Release Notes

text: Skeletal mesh animation pose no longer resets when you edit a property on a component (subobject) of the actor. Fixed not being able to set just the X, Y, or Z channels of a transform for a skeletal mesh. Fix issue with baking code (and other code) that uses FindSpawnableObjectTemplate in the case that the guid passed in is a possessable that is possessing a spawnable in another sequence. We now check for that. Fix crash when closing Sequencer during deferred modification flush We do this by suppressing the deferred modification flush events during the destructor. Fix crash when compiling sequences with null tracks Runs 'RemoveNullTracks) before calling CompileTrack() to prevent crashes when a sequence contains null track references. We need to track down what is causing tracks to be null, but this should fix the crash as it currently exists. Fix Control Rig ECS crash that happens with dynamic rigs that change the control rig channels mid evaluation. To fix this we hold a hash of the channel list in the control rig component data and if it changes we re-copy the channel pointers into the ecs component or unlink if channels no longer exist. . Sections with no channels are again considered keyable (regression fix for keyable detection). text: Splitting or trimming a section now places boundary keys with the correct values and preserves each key's original interpolation type, so a linear curve stays linear instead of being forced into a cubic S‑curve. Fixed crash when a level sequence has a null track. Fixed a crash that could occur when evaluating sequences with transform origins gathered from multiple subscenes in parallel. A Template Sequence section's Hierarchical Bias now initializes before config can overwrite it, so per-section overrides stick instead of inheriting the config default. The viewport no longer jitters when the aspect ratio is animated. Sequence players set to loop now remember their loop count after playback ends. Restarting a looping sequence plays as a loop instead of playing once and stopping. Camera Cuts and other pinned tracks no longer disappear from the timeline when dragged into a folder. Sequencer now blocks drops into folders with a mismatched pinned state and shows no drop preview. Editing the Level Sequence Actor's Transform Origin now marks the sequence dirty so the editor re-evaluates it. Whether using anim Blueprints or custom mode, the previous anim instance gets force re-initialized after sequence is over, potentially resetting data stored in the AnimInstance unnecessarily. Previously this would only occur if the skeleton changed, but we attempted to address an issue where if Custom Mode was used, the previous anim instance was getting uninitialized anyway, and would now be stuck in an uninitialized case. That fix was a bit overzealous however, as this forced re-initialization was even occurring for cases where animation Blueprints were used and we weren't switching anim mode or anim instances. This change only re-initializes if Sequencer changed (and is now restoring) the anim instance. Fragment type strings for the Universal Object Locator are now encoded/decoded so characters that are illegal in object names survive serialization. The audio track no longer crashes when its played from an Actor Sequence. Dragging the time range slider now properly accounts for display scaling on the desktop. Resolving setter functions for bool properties now strips off the leading 'b' (eg. SetVisible matches the bVisible property).

Results will be written to Saved/MultiprocessResults/results.txt, the location of results can be overridden with the `-resultsfile=` option. -numworkers= can be used to control the number of workers used to process the batch. Batch jobs can also be started from script using `BatchProcessLibrary::RunBatch`. Editor Preview Platform Optimizations Materials are already updated by SetPreviewPlatform, so disable the automatic per-texture material dependency update 8min →1min Preview transition. Improved support for incremental validation in incremental cooks. Incremental cooks already mostly handle incremental validation, as they skip loading the package if it hasn't changed (as validation runs via UCookOnTheFlyServer::LoadPackageInQueue), however changes to a world would still validate all their external objects. This can be quite slow for large worlds. This change improves the incremental validation support so that it only validates the specific external objects that have changed in a world being re-cooked. It does this by comparing the hash of each external actor object against the previous version that was validated, and skipping any that haven't changed.

This was because the viewport's camera controller was clamping the pitch angle to -90;+90 degrees, so when that came into effect, the output pitch differed from the input pitch. This in turn was picked up by the viewport's camera movement handling as a difference that needed to be reproduced on the locked actor, something that happens when piloting an actor using a movement mode that has inertia for smoother movements. This change just disables that part of the code when input is itself disabled (which is the case in the PiP viewports), since it makes little sense to move a locked actor if the user doesn't have input to pilot it. The USD Interchange import option for filtering imported geometry purposes has moved back to the USD Translator settings (it temporarily became a USD Pipeline option). Interchange USD now supports prim collapsing, both via prim kinds and the dedicated collapsing schemas. The collapsing settings can be configured on the USD Translator settings (the three dots on the top right of the USD Interchange import options dialog). Improved support for camera parameters when importing via USD Interchange, expanding support for clip planes, exposure method, exposure compensation value, and exposure FStop, ISO and shutter speed attributes. Actors, components and assets imported via USD Interchange will only have their properties set to any value if the corresponding source USD attribute had an actually authored opinion. In other words, fallback USD values will no longer be converted into Unreal property values. Refactored the USD Translator to use Schema Handlers: These are classes meant to each describe the translation of a particular USD schema. Users can implement, override, disable, enable and reorder schema handlers from project-level code and plugins, and e.g. implement translation of their custom USD schemas for USD Interchange.

Interactive Tools Framework: Modified UInteractiveToolPropertySet::SaveRestoreProperties to only instantiate a property cache entry when saving. This permits successive calls to RestoreProperties to behave as expected, particularly in the case where a tool inherits from a base tool class, but wants to modify the defaults of an inherited property set. In that scenario, both the base class and derived class would issue RestoreProperties on the inherited property set. Prior to this change, the first call to RestoreProperties would instantiate the property cache and detect that the property cache was just created to avoid the restore. The second call to RestoreProperties would incorrectly see the just created property cache as evidence that there is saved data to restore and copy the default CDO data to the tool. By only instantiating the property cache on save operations, the behavior is more consistent and avoids tools having to create awkward workarounds using separate property cache IDs to workaround the issue. Adding FMA intrinsics when compiling with MinimumCpuArchitectureX64.AVX2 on Clang. This fixes a compile error in the Eigen library when compiling AVX2 on Dedicated Servers using Clang. This is because when compiling using the VCToolChain using Clang, we still define _MSC_VER so the Eigen library assumes FMA is included because MSVC always includes those intrinsics when using /arch:Avx2. This change brings our Clang configuration in line with MSVC when using AVX2. Note that this does not change the ffp-contract behaviour, so will not allow the compiler to optimise multiply add operations automatically.
